_note: Rice volumes are MILLED-basis, thousand metric tonnes (kt), unless a flow note says otherwise. Trade is reported on a calendar-year basis; most exporter/importer totals are USDA FAS PSD 2024 (Jan 2025 release) with bilateral splits from national customs / ITC Trade Map / WITS-Comtrade. India's July-2023 to Sept-2024 export restrictions on non-basmati white rice are the dominant recent structural event.

IND.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: India milled production ~147,000 kt (now #1, ahead of China), consumption ~120,000 kt. CY2024 exports ~17,000 kt (~40% of world trade) despite the non-basmati white-rice ban that ran Jul-2023 to Sep-2024.

CHN.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: China milled production ~145,300 kt, consumption ~150,000 kt. Exports ~1,600 kt (mostly to Africa/Korea/PNG); imports ~1,700 kt (down sharply from 2021-22 peaks as TRQ fragrant/broken demand eased).

BGD.note: USDA: Bangladesh milled production ~37,000 kt. FY2024/25 imports surged to ~2,650 kt (2nd highest globally) after flood/production shortfalls; near-entirely from India.

IDN.note: USDA/Indonesia customs: production ~33,000 kt. 2024 imports spiked to ~4,520 kt (Bulog buying on El Niño-hit harvest), the year's largest single-country import jump; main suppliers Thailand, Vietnam, Myanmar, Pakistan.

VNM.note: USDA/Vietnam customs: production ~27,000 kt. 2024 exports a record ~9,000 kt (Philippines is ~45% of that); also imports ~1,100 kt of Cambodian/Indian paddy for re-milling.

THA.note: USDA/Thai Rice Exporters Assoc.: production ~20,300 kt milled. 2024 exports ~9,900-10,000 kt (white, parboiled, Hom Mali fragrant) — boosted by India's ban; Africa a record buyer.

PAK.note: USDA PSD: Pakistan production ~10,000 kt milled. 2024 exports ~5,900 kt (basmati to Gulf/EU, non-basmati to Africa/SE Asia) — record on India-gap demand.

USA.note: USDA PSD MY2024/25: US milled production ~7,700 kt. Exports ~2,800-3,000 kt (long-grain to Mexico/Haiti/C.America, medium-grain to N.Asia/MENA); imports ~1,400 kt of aromatic (Thai jasmine, Indian basmati).

MMR.note: USDA PSD: Myanmar/Burma production ~12,500 kt. 2024 exports ~2,200-2,400 kt — undercutting India on cheap non-basmati white rice to China, EU, Africa, Philippines, Indonesia.

KHM.note: USDA/Cambodia: production ~8,200 kt. Milled-rice exports ~700 kt (premium fragrant to EU/China) but >3,000 kt of paddy crosses informally to Vietnam/Thailand; PSD exportable surplus ~2,000 kt.

BRA.note: USDA PSD: Brazil production ~7,900 kt. Exports ~1,300 kt (to Latin America, W.Africa, Iran); also imports ~700-900 kt from Mercosur (Paraguay, Uruguay, Argentina) in deficit years.

URY.note: USDA/Uruguay: production ~960 kt milled, almost all exported (~900 kt) — Brazil, Peru, Mexico, Iraq, EU the main markets.

PRY.note: USDA/Paraguay: production ~1,050 kt milled; exports ~900 kt, mostly to Brazil and the rest of South America.

ARG.note: USDA/Argentina: production ~1,000 kt milled; exports ~650-700 kt to Brazil, Chile, Mexico, EU.

ITA.note: Eurostat/Ente Nazionale Risi: Italy is the EU's biggest producer (~1,000 kt milled, Po Valley japonica/Arborio). Exports ~750 kt within EU + to MENA; imports indica for milling.

PHL.note: USDA/PSA: Philippines production ~12,300 kt milled, consumption ~16,500 kt. 2024 imports a record ~4,700 kt — the world's #1 rice importer; ~80% from Vietnam.

NGA.note: USDA: Nigeria milled production ~5,400 kt, consumption ~7,500 kt. Imports ~2,000-2,100 kt (much via Benin/Togo transshipment); India parboiled the traditional staple, Thai gaining.

CIV.note: USDA/Côte d'Ivoire customs: production ~1,500 kt milled; imports ~1,600-1,700 kt — West Africa's largest white-rice buyer; suppliers Vietnam, India, Pakistan, Thailand, China.

SEN.note: Senegal customs: 2024 imports ~1,380 kt ($564.7m, +4.3% YoY); top suppliers Thailand (31% by value), India (28%), Pakistan (17.6%) — heavily broken rice.

IRQ.note: USDA: Iraq imports ~1,300-1,400 kt — India (basmati & non-basmati), Uruguay, USA, Brazil are main suppliers via government tenders.

SAU.note: USDA: Saudi Arabia imports ~1,500-1,600 kt, almost entirely Indian basmati (now India's #1 basmati market, having overtaken Iran); some re-exports across the Gulf.

IRN.note: USDA: Iran production ~2,300 kt; imports ~1,200-1,500 kt of Indian/Pakistani basmati, subject to periodic seasonal import bans to protect domestic growers.

EU.note: USDA/Eurostat: EU-27 milled production ~1,500 kt (Italy, Spain). 2024/25 imports ~2,200-2,400 kt — Cambodia, Myanmar, Pakistan, India, Thailand; entering via Rotterdam, Antwerp, Hamburg.

MYS.note: WITS-Comtrade/Bernas: Malaysia 2024 imports ~1,300 kt — Vietnam ~39%, Pakistan ~21%, India ~21%, Thailand ~13%, Cambodia ~5% (by value).

GHA.note: USDA: Ghana milled production ~900 kt; imports ~900-1,000 kt — Vietnam, India, Thailand the main suppliers.

ZAF.note: South Africa grows almost no rice; 2024 imports ~1,000-1,100 kt, with Thailand the dominant supplier (833 kt of Thai rice in 2024, a record) plus India; re-exports to neighbours.

CHL.note: WITS-Comtrade: Chile imports ~300 kt, mostly from Argentina, Paraguay, Brazil, USA. Production/consumption are USDA-bracketed estimates.

MEX.note: USDA: Mexico milled production ~130 kt; imports ~850-900 kt, ~80% US long-grain (mostly rough/paddy milled domestically), some Uruguay/Paraguay.

JPN.note: USDA: Japan production ~7,300 kt; imports ~680-700 kt under WTO minimum-access TRQ, chiefly US and Thai; 2025 shortage prompted extra spot buying.

KOR.note: USDA: South Korea production ~3,600 kt; imports ~410-450 kt under TRQ — China, USA, Vietnam, Thailand.

EGY.note: USDA: Egypt production ~4,800 kt (japonica/medium-grain). Exports ~300 kt (to Turkey, MENA) when not export-banned for water reasons; small imports in deficit years.

AFG.note: WITS-Comtrade: Afghanistan imports ~500-600 kt, predominantly Pakistani non-basmati overland; balance USDA-bracketed.

NPL.note: Nepal imports ~600-700 kt, almost entirely from India overland; balance USDA/FAO-bracketed.

TUR.note: Türkiye imports ~500-700 kt (USA, Russia, India, Egypt) and re-exports milled rice to neighbours; balance Comtrade/USDA-bracketed.

MOZ.note: Mozambique imports ~600-700 kt; Thailand a major supplier (287 kt of Thai rice in 2024) plus India, Pakistan.

BEN.note: Benin is a transit hub: imports ~1,200-1,400 kt (India, Thailand) and re-exports ~600 kt informally into Nigeria; figures Comtrade/USDA-bracketed and known to be understated by informal flows.

Thailand shipped ~498-598 kt to the Philippines in 2024, the #2 supplier (Philippine Bureau of Plant Industry/PSA).
Pakistan supplied ~284 kt to the Philippines in 2024 (PSA).
Myanmar shipped ~67-143 kt to the Philippines in 2024 (PSA).
Thailand supplied ~1,364 kt to Indonesia in 2024, the top supplier in the import-spike year (Indonesia customs / WITS-Comtrade).
Vietnam shipped ~1,248 kt to Indonesia in 2024 (Indonesia customs / WITS-Comtrade).
Myanmar supplied ~831 kt to Indonesia in 2024 (Indonesia customs / WITS-Comtrade).
Pakistan shipped ~804 kt to Indonesia in 2024 (Indonesia customs / WITS-Comtrade).
India supplied the remainder (~270 kt) of Indonesia's record 4.52 Mt 2024 import total (Indonesia customs / WITS-Comtrade).

Iraq buys ~0.8-1.0 Mt of Indian rice (basmati + non-basmati) via state tenders (APEDA / Iraq trade).

India was ~28% of Senegal's 2024 rice imports by value (~0.35 Mt), behind Thailand (Senegal customs / Ecofin).
India supplies essentially all of Nepal's ~0.6-0.7 Mt imports overland (WITS-Comtrade; basis: Nepal has no other land supplier).
India a major supplier to South Africa alongside Thailand; ~0.2-0.3 Mt (WITS-Comtrade).
India ships ~0.2-0.3 Mt of basmati/aromatic rice to the US ethnic market (APEDA).
India supplies basmati and non-basmati to the EU within tariff-rate quotas; ~0.3 Mt (Eurostat/CBI).
Yemen and other MENA states take Indian non-basmati and basmati; ~0.3 Mt (APEDA basis: India's MENA non-Gulf book).
South Africa led Thai-rice growth in 2024 with ~833 kt, a record (Thai Rice Exporters Association).
Senegal took ~462 kt of Thai rice in 2024 — Thailand was Senegal's #1 supplier (31% by value) (Thai Rice Exporters Assoc.).
Côte d'Ivoire imported ~311 kt of Thai rice in 2024 (Thai Rice Exporters Assoc.).
Benin imported ~287 kt of Thai rice in 2024, much for onward Nigeria trade (Thai Rice Exporters Assoc.).
Mozambique imported ~287 kt of Thai rice in 2024 (Thai Rice Exporters Assoc.).
Iraq buys Thai parboiled/white rice via tenders alongside Indian and Uruguayan; ~0.25 Mt (USDA basis).
Thai jasmine/fragrant rice to the US is the largest aromatic-import line (~0.45 Mt) (US Census / Comtrade).
China imported ~433 kt of Thai rice in 2024 (US$295m), its top single supplier by value (China customs / WITS).
Thailand is a leading WTO-TRQ supplier to Japan (~0.2-0.3 Mt), rising on Japan's 2024/25 shortfall (USDA).
Vietnam was Côte d'Ivoire's #1 supplier in 2023 (~US$314m, ~0.5 Mt) (OEC / Côte d'Ivoire customs).
Vietnam is a leading supplier to Ghana (~0.4 Mt) alongside India and Thailand (WITS-Comtrade).
Malaysia imported ~688 kt from Vietnam in 2024 (~39% of imports by value), its top supplier (WITS-Comtrade).
China imported ~281 kt of Vietnamese rice in 2024 (US$165m) (China customs / WITS).
China imported ~159 kt of Pakistani rice in 2024 (US$74m) (China customs / WITS).
Pakistan is a leading non-basmati supplier to Kenya and East Africa (~0.3 Mt) (WITS-Comtrade basis).
Malaysia imported ~382 kt from Pakistan in 2024 (~21% by value), its #2 supplier (WITS-Comtrade).
Pakistan supplies the bulk of Afghanistan's ~0.5 Mt imports overland (WITS-Comtrade; basis: dominant land route).
Pakistan exported ~450 kt of rice to Europe in 2023 (basmati + non-basmati); ~0.35-0.45 Mt typical (CBI/Eurostat).
Pakistan was ~17.6% of Senegal's 2024 rice imports by value (~0.24 Mt) (Senegal customs / Ecofin).
China imported ~564 kt of Myanmar rice in 2024 (US$267m), its top supplier by VOLUME (much over-border/broken) (China customs / WITS).
Myanmar is a major EU supplier of Indica white/broken rice (~0.3-0.4 Mt), at times under EU safeguard tariffs (Eurostat).
Myanmar non-basmati white rice into West Africa (Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea); ~0.2 Mt (WITS-Comtrade).
Mexico is the US's #1 rice market — ~0.6-0.8 Mt of long-grain (much shipped rough and milled in Mexico) (USDA FAS GATS).
Haiti is a top US long-grain market (~0.4 Mt), heavily import-dependent (USDA FAS GATS).
US medium-grain to Japan under the WTO minimum-access TRQ (~0.3-0.4 Mt) (USDA FAS GATS).
Canada buys ~0.15-0.2 Mt of US milled rice (USDA FAS GATS).

US long-grain into Iraq via tenders (~0.1-0.2 Mt), variable year to year (USDA basis).
China re-exports/exports rice to West Africa (Côte d'Ivoire ~US$24m in 2023 plus larger non-basmati books); ~0.3 Mt (WITS-Comtrade).
China supplies South Korea's TRQ (~0.2 Mt) (WITS-Comtrade).
Cambodia exported ~243 kt of (mostly fragrant) rice to the EU in 2023, rising; the EU is its top milled-rice market (Eurostat/CBI).
China is Cambodia's other large milled-rice buyer under a bilateral quota (~0.25 Mt) (China customs / WITS).
Brazil exports milled rice to Peru and other Andean/W.African markets; ~0.2 Mt (WITS-Comtrade).
Paraguay's largest rice market is Brazil (~0.6 Mt) (WITS-Comtrade / Paraguay customs).

Guinea and other West African states take Indian non-basmati; ~0.3 Mt (WITS-Comtrade basis).

rankings.note: Exporter/importer bar values are milled-basis kt for calendar-year 2024, from USDA FAS PSD (Jan 2025 release) cross-checked against national customs and ITC Trade Map / WITS-Comtrade. India ~17,000 kt = ~40% of the ~56-60 Mt world trade. Indonesia's 4,500 kt is a 2024 spike (El Niño harvest hit); its normal level is far lower.

companies.name: Olam Agri
companies.metric: Trades >40 Mt of agri commodities/yr; one of the largest global rice merchandisers; secured US$100m (2025) to expand Africa rice shipments.
companies.note: Major originator and shipper of rice into Africa and the Middle East; origination hubs in Nigeria, Vietnam and Thailand. Olam announced a 2024 combination with Louis Dreyfus's rice business, pooling origination.
companies.improve: Should publish origin-split rice volumes and the share of parboiled vs white vs fragrant it moves, so its exposure to an India-style export ban can be sized rather than inferred.

companies.name: Louis Dreyfus Company (LDC)
companies.metric: One of the ABCD majors; dedicated global Rice platform (merchandising + milling). 2024 Olam-LDC rice combination created a ~US$40bn-revenue origination platform.
companies.note: Long-standing global rice merchandiser with milling and origination across Asia and the Americas; supplies Africa, the Middle East and the EU.
companies.improve: Rice-segment volumes are not broken out in group reporting; disclosing origin and destination concentration would let food-security analysts model supplier-shock exposure.

companies.name: ITC Limited (Agri Business)
companies.metric: ~9.8% share of India's rice exports (Feb 2025); supplies basmati & non-basmati to the Gulf, US, SE Asia and EU.
companies.note: India's largest single rice exporter by share; sources paddy across Indian states and ships premium basmati and bulk non-basmati. Directly exposed to India's export-policy switches.
companies.improve: Concentration in a single origin (India) makes ITC's rice book highly sensitive to New Delhi's ban/MEP/duty changes — it should disclose how it hedges policy risk.

companies.name: KRBL Limited (India Gate basmati)
companies.metric: World's largest basmati rice miller/exporter by brand; flagship India Gate; exports to >90 countries (Gulf, US, EU).
companies.note: Dominant branded basmati exporter; the Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Iran) is its core market — directly exposed to India's basmati MEP and to Gulf demand swings.
companies.improve: Should disclose destination-market concentration (Gulf share) and basmati MEP sensitivity for investors sizing geopolitical/policy risk.

companies.name: Phoenix Group (Pakistan)
companies.metric: One of Pakistan's largest rice exporters (basmati + non-basmati); ships to the Gulf, EU, Africa and SE Asia.
companies.note: Representative of the Pakistani exporter cluster (REAP members) that captured India-gap demand in 2023-24. Volume figures are not publicly audited — flagged modeled.
companies.improve: Pakistani exporters as a group lack audited public volumes; a sourced REAP member-level disclosure would let analysts quantify Pakistan's swing-supplier role.

companies.name: CP Intertrade / Thai exporter cluster
companies.metric: Thailand exported ~9.9-10 Mt in 2024; CP Intertrade (Royal Umbrella) and the Thai Rice Exporters Association members dominate fragrant/parboiled shipments.
companies.note: Stands in for Thailand's major branded exporters (CP, Asia Golden Rice, Thai Hua, etc.). Africa was a record 3 Mt Thai-rice market in 2024.
companies.improve: Company-level Thai export volumes are not consistently public; TREA member disclosure would sharpen exposure mapping for African import-dependent states.

global.note: World milled-rice totals, kt, USDA FAS PSD (production & consumption on a milled basis; trade calendar-year). Global trade peaked ~55.9 Mt in 2022, dipped in 2023 on India's ban, and recovered to ~56-60 Mt in 2024-25 after the ban was lifted. 2024/25 production is a record (~535 Mt), India now the #1 producer (~147 Mt) ahead of China (~145 Mt).

forecast.method: Projected 2030 value = 2024 value × (1 + CAGR)^6, per metric. Net = projected production − projected consumption. CAGR figures are reasoned assumptions inside the OECD-FAO Agricultural Outlook 2024-2033 envelope (global rice demand +~1%/yr, with Africa the fastest-growing import region and Asian per-capita consumption flat-to-declining). Stated openly so they can be challenged.

scenarios.label: India re-imposes a non-basmati white-rice export ban
scenarios.note: Modeled on the actual Jul-2023 to Sep-2024 ban: Indian shipments fell ~one-third (from 21.3 Mt to 14.3 Mt Sep23-Aug24, non-basmati white rice down ~87%) and the Thai 5% price rose ~20%. Africa, Bangladesh and SE Asia are hit hardest; India is ~40% of world trade so a partial ban removes the largest swing supplier.

scenarios.label: El Niño cuts SE-Asian harvests, Indonesia/Philippines import surge
scenarios.note: The 2023-24 El Niño drove Indonesia's 2024 imports to a record ~4.52 Mt and the Philippines to ~4.7 Mt. A repeat tightens exportable supply from Thailand/Vietnam and lifts prices for all import-dependent buyers.

scenarios.label: Vietnam restricts exports to protect domestic supply
scenarios.note: Vietnam has briefly suspended/limited rice export contracts before (e.g. 2020). As the Philippines' ~80% supplier and #2 world exporter, even a temporary Vietnamese curb leaves Manila acutely exposed.

scenarios.label: Gulf shipping/sanctions disruption hits India-Pakistan basmati to MENA
scenarios.note: ~80% of India's basmati goes to the Middle East (Saudi Arabia now #1, plus Iran, Iraq, UAE). Red Sea/Strait-of-Hormuz disruption or Iran sanctions/payment friction has already curbed basmati flows; models a hit to the premium export trade.

scenarios.label: Thai drought cuts exportable rice ~20%
scenarios.note: Thailand's irrigated-area and reservoir swings move exportable supply ~15-25% between years. As the #2 exporter and Africa's record 2024 supplier (~3 Mt), a Thai shortfall raises West-African and MENA import costs.

scenarios.label: Pakistan flood destroys rice crop (2022-style)
scenarios.note: The 2022 floods cut Pakistan's rice output sharply and slashed exports. As the swing supplier that absorbed India-ban demand (Gulf basmati, African/SE-Asian non-basmati), a Pakistani shortfall removes the main alternative to India.

rice.label: All rice (HS 1006)
rice.note: All rice — the default view: paddy, husked/brown, semi/wholly milled, and broken, milled-basis kt (USDA FAS PSD / ITC).

white.label: Milled white & parboiled (HS 100630)
white.note: Semi- or wholly-milled rice (HS 100630) — the bulk of world trade (~80-85% by weight), including India's non-basmati white, Thai/Vietnamese white, and parboiled for Africa (ITC Trade Map 2024).

basmati.label: Aromatic / basmati
basmati.note: Premium long-grain aromatic — Indian & Pakistani basmati (to the Gulf, EU, US) plus Thai Hom Mali jasmine. ~10-14% of trade by weight but a far larger share by value (APEDA / Thai Rice Exporters Assoc.).

broken.label: Broken rice (HS 100640)
broken.note: Broken rice (HS 100640) — a key West-African and brewing/feed staple; Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire and China are big buyers. ~10-15% of trade by weight (ITC Trade Map 2024).

paddy.label: Paddy / rough rice (HS 100610)
paddy.note: Rough/paddy rice (HS 100610) — milled at destination. Big routes: US→Mexico and US→C.America rough rice; large informal Cambodia→Vietnam and Cambodia→Thailand paddy flows. Volumes here are illustrative milled-equivalent.
